title: Section 108 CPC - Procedure in appeals from appellate decrees and orders

content.overview: Section 108 CPC - Procedure in appeals from appellate decrees and orders. Civil-procedure treatise covering statutory anatomy, mandatory conditions, forum, limitation, connected provisions, judicial authority and chamber drafting.
content.study:
Introduction and meaning
Section 108 CPC of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 is titled “Procedure in appeals from appellate decrees and orders”. Cluster: Appeals — general.
Section 108 CPC is titled “Procedure in appeals from appellate decrees and orders”. It belongs to Appeals — general. The student must write the working rule, the person who moves the court, the conditions, and the consequence if the conditions fail.

Doctrinal and Practice Scope
A concise legal assessment requires meaning, essentials, one illustration and leading authority. Comprehensive written submissions require IRAC problem analysis, neighbour distinctions, and a failure scenario.

Essentials of the provision
1. Cite Section 108 CPC and state the title in one line.
2. Name the connected Order if the facts are procedural.
3. What is under challenge — decree or order
4. Which section opens the appeal
5. What questions that court may decide
6. Apply the facts. If one condition is missing, say the heading fails.

Statutory Illustration (applies)
A party relies on Section 108 CPC (Procedure in appeals from appellate decrees and orders) at the proper stage of a civil suit. Every condition of the heading is present. The court applies Section 108 CPC and grants the procedural consequence the section or Order provides.

Counter-Illustration (fails)
The same party uses Section 108 CPC at the wrong stage, or against a stranger, or where a more specific CPC heading already occupies the field. Section 108 CPC is then not attracted. State that failure clearly — it is the crucial distinction in chamber practice.

Landmark Judicial Authority
1. Santosh Hazari v. Purushottam Tiwari (2001), (2001) 3 SCC 179: Second appeal needs a substantial question of law.
2. Banarsi v. Ram Phal (2003), (2003) 1 SCC 727: First appeal is the last court of fact.

Connected provisions & distinctions
s. 96 first appeal; s. 100 second appeal; s. 104 orders; Order XLI / XLIII.

Current-law status
Cite Section 108 CPC of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908. CPC was not replaced by BNSS.

Dispatcher compliance
Section 108 CPC - Procedure in appeals from appellate decrees and orders must be read as part of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, which remains in force and is not repealed by BNSS. Distinguish a substantive CPC section from an Order and Rule. Identify the stage of the civil suit, the competent court, the pleading or application before the Court, the limitation or case-management deadline, and the precise procedural order sought.

Civil litigation proof and procedural fairness
The party asserting the procedural foundation must establish it from the pleadings, orders, service record and admissible documents. Where electronic filings, notices, orders or account records are relied upon, check the applicable BSA 2023 route, including ss. 63, 104 and 109 where relevant. Electronic evidence does not cure defective service, lack of jurisdiction, limitation or failure to plead a material fact.

Senior Counsel close
Apply the CPC provision in sequence: identify the cause of action or procedural stage, read the exact statutory or Order/Rule language, test jurisdiction and limitation, distinguish the nearest procedural remedy, apply the facts, and seek a precise order. Avoid treating procedural rules as automatic dismissal unless the Code or binding authority makes that consequence mandatory.
